10 Johnson ST

Newtown

Dear Ms Graham

Re: Mr Barry Jones

DOB: 01/04/1972

I am writing this letter to refer Mr Jones, a 44-year-old forklift driver, who has been suffering from back
pain. Your assessment would be highly appreciated.

Mr Jones is married and has 3 children. Regarding his work situation, his work requires him to sit for
prolonged periods and to lift heavy objects.

On 21/03/2015, Mr Jones came complaining of 4-days worsening occupational back pain after lifting a
heavy box. Thus, he was commenced on Naproxen and Carisoprodol and was recommended on gradual
daily walking. In addition, he was given a one month work vacation. In the two subsequent visits, he was
still complaining of back pain. Therefore, his Naproxen dose was increased.

On today's review, Mr Jones attended my surgery as his back was recovering. However, still painful. The
pain was particularly after sitting or laying down more than 20 to 30 minutes associated with stiffly
movement with increase in his ROM. Moreover, he was jogging 30 minutes daily. Nonetheless, it was tiring
to him. Upon discussion, the patient was restless, discouraged and wants to return to his work.
